name: China (Mainland)
summary: Mainland China is a heavily codified, employee-protective regime: there is no at-will employment, every unilateral termination must fit a Labor Contract Law ground, and wrongful dismissal costs double severance (2N) or reinstatement. National law (Labor Law, Labor Contract Law, Social Insurance Law, PIPL) is overlaid by city rules that differ materially between Shanghai and Shenzhen (leave, sick pay, social insurance bases, minimum wage), and 2025-26 brought a wave of change: gradual retirement-age increases, 13 public holidays, SPC Interpretation II on labor disputes, MOHRSS non-compete guidelines, and Shanghai's sick-pay reset. US-HQ semiconductor employers most often get wrong: treating performance exits as at-will, enforcing a global handbook that never went through China's democratic procedure, paying social insurance on a reduced base, using non-competes without monthly compensation, moving HR data to US systems without PIPL notices and separate consents, and granting RSUs without SAFE Circular 7 registration. Export-control, counter-espionage and anti-sanctions rules add a security layer that HR must coordinate with trade compliance.

ratingNotes.termination: Closed list of statutory grounds, union pre-notification, protected categories, 2N or reinstatement for errors; exits are in practice negotiated.
ratingNotes.representation: Only ACFTU unions; 2% union funds and democratic procedure for rules are mandatory, but unions in foreign-invested tech firms are usually cooperative and collective bargaining is limited.
ratingNotes.privacy: PIPL with separate-consent rules, cross-border transfer regime, PIPIAs, compliance audits, PIPO registration, plus DSL/CSL and state-secret/counter-espionage overlay.
ratingNotes.payTransparency: No pay-range disclosure or pay-gap reporting law; equal-pay-for-equal-work and gender non-discrimination principles apply.
ratingNotes.workingTime: Strict OT caps (36 h/month) and 150/200/300% premiums; exempt-style arrangements require government approval of special working hour systems.
ratingNotes.leave: Statutory annual leave is modest, but maternity/childcare leave, medical treatment periods and local variations (Shanghai vs Guangdong) add complexity.
ratingNotes.immigration: Work permit (A/B/C tiers) + Z visa + residence permit sequence is paper-heavy but predictable; foreigners must join social insurance.
ratingNotes.changeVelocity: Frequent national and municipal changes in 2025-26 (retirement age, holidays, SPC Interpretation II, non-compete guidelines, Shanghai sick pay, data rules).

keyFacts.label: Employment model
keyFacts.value: No at-will employment: the employer may end employment only by mutual agreement, contract expiry or statutory grounds in Labor Contract Law (LCL) Arts. 36, 39, 40, 41 and 44; anything else risks 2N damages or reinstatement. Local staff must be employed by a PRC entity (here the WFOE) or via licensed dispatch/HR agency.

keyFacts.label: Contracts & offer letters
keyFacts.value: Written labor contract must be signed within one month of start; otherwise double wages from month 2 (up to 11 months) and, after 1 year, a deemed open-ended contract (LCL Arts. 10, 14, 82). After 10 years' service or two consecutive fixed terms the employee can demand an open-ended contract; SPC Interpretation II Art. 10 treats extensions totaling 1+ year, automatic renewals and employer-driven entity switches as consecutive terms.

keyFacts.label: Probation
keyFacts.value: Contract 3 months to <1 year: max 1 month; 1 to <3 years: max 2 months; 3+ years or open-ended: max 6 months; none for contracts under 3 months; one probation per employee per employer (LCL Art. 19). Probation pay at least 80% of agreed wage and not below local minimum wage; probation dismissal still requires documented failure of pre-disclosed hiring criteria.

keyFacts.label: Notice (employer)
keyFacts.value: None for Art. 39 fault dismissals. Art. 40 no-fault terminations need 30 days' written notice or one month's wage in lieu (the '+1' in N+1). Mass layoffs (Art. 41) require a 30-day explanation to the union or all employees and a report to the labor bureau; the union must be notified before any unilateral termination (Art. 43).

keyFacts.label: Notice (employee)
keyFacts.value: 30 days' written notice (3 days during probation); no employer acceptance needed and longer contractual notice is generally unenforceable. Employee may resign immediately and claim severance if the employer breaches (e.g., unpaid wages, no social insurance) under LCL Art. 38.

keyFacts.label: Statutory severance
keyFacts.value: Economic compensation (N): one month's wage per full year; 6-12 months counts as one year; under 6 months = half a month; wage = average of prior 12 months incl. bonuses/allowances. If monthly wage exceeds 3x the local average monthly wage, the rate is capped at 3x and years at 12 (LCL Art. 47). Unlawful termination: 2N (Art. 87) or reinstatement with back pay.

keyFacts.label: Working hours & overtime
keyFacts.value: Standard 8 hours/day, 40 hours/week; overtime normally max 1 h/day, 3 h/day in special cases, 36 h/month (Labor Law Art. 41). Premiums: 150% workdays, 200% rest days (or time off), 300% public holidays. Comprehensive or flexible (non-fixed) hour systems require local HR bureau approval.

keyFacts.label: Minimum wage
keyFacts.value: Shanghai: RMB 2,740/month and RMB 25/hour since 1 Jul 2025 (no 2026 increase issued as of Sept 2026), excluding OT, shift/meal/transport/housing allowances and employee social insurance/housing fund contributions. Shenzhen: RMB 2,700/month and RMB 25.4/hour from 1 Sept 2026 (previously RMB 2,520).

keyFacts.label: Annual leave
keyFacts.value: 5 / 10 / 15 working days for cumulative (all-employer) work experience of 1-<10 / 10-<20 / 20+ years, after 12 months' continuous work; pro-rated for joiners and leavers. Untaken leave not waived by the employee in writing is paid at 300% of daily wage (Regulations on Paid Annual Leave for Employees 2008 and 2008 Implementation Measures).

keyFacts.label: Public holidays
keyFacts.value: 13 days from 1 Jan 2025 (Spring Festival Eve and 2 May added): New Year 1, Spring Festival 4, Qingming 1, Labor Day 2, Dragon Boat 1, Mid-Autumn 1, National Day 3. The State Council publishes a yearly schedule with swapped weekend workdays; MOHRSS now uses 20.67 average working days/month and 21.75 pay days/month for wage conversion.

keyFacts.label: Sick leave
keyFacts.value: Job-protected medical treatment period of 3-24 months by service (national 1994 rules; Shanghai uses its own service-based table). Sick pay floor is 80% of local minimum wage; Shenzhen requires at least 60% of normal wage. Shanghai's 1995/2000 sick-pay notices lapsed on 15 Aug 2026, so Shanghai sick pay now follows contract/handbook terms subject to the 80% floor (about RMB 2,192).

keyFacts.label: Parental leave
keyFacts.value: National maternity leave 98 days (15 prenatal; +15 difficult birth; +15 per additional baby). Shanghai adds 60 days (158 total), 10 days paternity and 5 days/year childcare leave per parent until the child turns 3; Guangdong/Shenzhen adds 80 days (178 total), 15 days paternity and 10 days/year childcare leave per parent until age 3. Maternity allowance comes from maternity insurance; employers top up where it is below salary under local rules.

keyFacts.label: Social insurance / mandatory benefits
keyFacts.value: Pension, medical (maternity merged), unemployment and work-injury insurance plus housing provident fund, mandatory for PRC and foreign employees, on prior-year average wage within city floor/cap. Shanghai base from 1 Jul 2026: RMB 7,546-37,731; employer roughly 16% pension, 9% medical, 0.5% unemployment, industry work-injury rate, 5-7% housing fund. Agreements waiving social insurance are void (SPC Interpretation II Art. 19).

keyFacts.label: Payroll frequency & final pay
keyFacts.value: Pay at least monthly in RMB on a fixed date with an itemized wage statement (Shanghai Enterprise Wage Payment Measures reissued effective 1 Aug 2026). Final wages are due in full at termination (verify any short local grace period in Shenzhen); economic compensation is payable when the handover is completed (LCL Art. 50).

keyFacts.label: Employee representation
keyFacts.value: Only ACFTU-affiliated unions are lawful; employees may form an enterprise union and the employer must pay union funds of 2% of total payroll (Trade Union Law), commonly collected by the tax bureau. Rules affecting vital interests require democratic procedure; the union must be notified before unilateral terminations; collective contracts are optional but encouraged.

keyFacts.label: Data privacy law
keyFacts.value: Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL, 2021), Data Security Law (2021), Cybersecurity Law (amended, effective 1 Jan 2026) and Network Data Security Management Regulations (effective 1 Jan 2025). HR processing may rely on necessity for HR management under lawful rules/collective contracts, but sensitive PI and cross-border transfers need separate consent, plus PIPIAs, compliance audits and PIPO registration above 1 million individuals.

keyFacts.label: Record retention
keyFacts.value: Keep texts of terminated/expired labor contracts at least 2 years (LCL Art. 50) and wage payment records at least 2 years (Interim Provisions on Wage Payment); PIPIA reports and processing records at least 3 years (PIPL Art. 56); payroll accounting vouchers 30 years under accounting archive rules. Employers bear the burden of proof for attendance and wage records they control.

keyFacts.label: Non-competes & IP
keyFacts.value: Post-employment non-competes only for senior management, senior technical staff and others with confidentiality duties, max 2 years, with monthly compensation paid after exit (LCL Arts. 23-24); MOHRSS Sept 2025 Guidelines: at least 30% of prior 12-month average pay (not below minimum wage), generally 50% if over one year. Interpretation II Art. 13 voids non-competes for staff without trade-secret access or with unreasonable scope. Service inventions belong to the employer (Patent Law Art. 6) but inventor reward and remuneration are mandatory.

keyFacts.label: Language requirements
keyFacts.value: No statute mandates Chinese-only documents, but labor bureaus, arbitration commissions and courts work in Chinese; use bilingual contracts and handbooks with Chinese prevailing and ensure employees can understand rules used against them. Foreign employees may have bilingual or English contracts.

keyFacts.label: Regulator(s)
keyFacts.value: MOHRSS and local HRSS bureaus (labor inspection, special-hour approvals, layoff filings); labor dispute arbitration commissions and People's Courts; State Taxation Administration (IIT and social insurance collection); Housing Provident Fund centers; Cyberspace Administration of China (PIPL); SAFE (equity plans/FX); science & technology bureaus and National Immigration Administration (work/residence permits); ACFTU.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Written labor contracts
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Written contract with statutory terms (term, job, work location, hours, pay, social insurance, labor protection) within one month of start and on every renewal; copy to employee.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Labor Contract Law Arts. 10, 17, 81, 82; SPC Interpretation II Arts. 6-11

mandatoryPolicies.name: Employee handbook / rules and regulations
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Rules on pay, hours, leave, safety, discipline, training etc. must be discussed with the employee congress or all employees, finalized after consultation with the union/employee representatives and publicized (signed acknowledgement) to be enforceable.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Labor Contract Law Art. 4; SPC Interpretation (I) on Labor Disputes (2020) Art. 50

mandatoryPolicies.name: Working hours and overtime policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Standard 8/40 schedule, OT caps (36 h/month), premium pay, OT approval and recording; special working hour systems only with HR bureau approval.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Labor Law Arts. 36-44; 1994 MOL Measures on Approval of Non-standard Working Hours

mandatoryPolicies.name: Annual leave policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: 5/10/15-day entitlement by cumulative service, scheduling, cross-year carry-over and 300% payment for untaken leave.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Regulations on Paid Annual Leave for Employees (2008) and Implementation Measures

mandatoryPolicies.name: Sick leave and medical treatment period policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Medical treatment period by service and sick pay levels; now essential in Shanghai, where sick pay follows contract/handbook terms after the 1995/2000 notices lapsed on 15 Aug 2026.
mandatoryPolicies.source: MOL 1994 Provisions on Medical Treatment Period; Shanghai 2015 medical period rules; local sick-pay rules

mandatoryPolicies.name: Maternity, paternity, childcare and marriage leave policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Align with national 98-day maternity leave and local population and family planning regulations (Shanghai, Guangdong) incl. pay/top-up of maternity allowance.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Special Provisions on Labor Protection of Female Employees (2012); Shanghai and Guangdong Population and Family Planning Regulations

mandatoryPolicies.name: Anti-sexual harassment system
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Employer must adopt rules, training, complaint channel, prompt investigation and handling, victim support and anti-retaliation measures.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Law on the Protection of Women's Rights and Interests (2022) Art. 25; Special Provisions on Labor Protection of Female Employees Art. 11

mandatoryPolicies.name: Female employee special protection
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: No dismissal or pay cut for pregnancy/maternity/nursing; no OT or night shifts from 7 months' pregnancy; prenatal checks on paid time; 1 hour/day nursing break until child is 1; no gender/marital/pregnancy questions or tests in hiring.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Special Provisions on Labor Protection of Female Employees (2012); Women's Rights Law (2022) Arts. 43-48

mandatoryPolicies.name: Employee personal information handling rules and privacy notice
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Notice of purposes, categories, retention, recipients and rights; HR-necessity basis documented in handbook/contract; separate consent for sensitive PI, third-party sharing and cross-border transfer.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Cross-border transfer compliance file
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Map HR data flows to US HQ/HRIS; rely on HR-management exemption where genuinely necessary, otherwise standard contract filing, certification or CAC security assessment by volume thresholds; PIPIA and separate consent.
mandatoryPolicies.source: PIPL Arts. 38-39; CAC Provisions on Promoting and Regulating Cross-Border Data Flows (Mar 2024); Certification Measures (effective 1 Jan 2026)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Personal information protection impact assessment (PIPIA)
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Before processing sensitive PI (health, biometrics, ID, bank data), cross-border transfers, entrusted processing (payroll vendors) and automated decisions; keep 3 years.
mandatoryPolicies.source: PIPL Arts. 55-56

mandatoryPolicies.name: PI compliance audits
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Periodic self-audits (mandatory every 2 years above 10 million individuals; risk-based otherwise) and regulator-ordered third-party audits.
mandatoryPolicies.source: PIPL Art. 54; Measures for PI Protection Compliance Audits (effective 1 May 2025)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Personal information protection officer
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Appoint and register with CAC a PIPO if processing PI of more than 1 million individuals (registration deadline was 29 Aug 2025; new crossers within 30 working days).
mandatoryPolicies.source: PIPL Art. 52; CAC 2025 PIPO reporting announcement

mandatoryPolicies.name: Data security incident response
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Incident plan, remediation and notification to authorities and affected individuals for PI breaches.
mandatoryPolicies.source: PIPL Art. 57; Network Data Security Management Regulations (2025); Cybersecurity Law (amended 2026)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Facial recognition / biometric attendance
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: If used for attendance or access: separate consent, non-biometric alternative, PIPIA, and filing with provincial CAC once 100,000+ individuals' face data is stored.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Security Management Measures for Application of Facial Recognition Technology (effective 1 Jun 2025)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Social insurance and housing fund enrollment
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Register within 30 days of hire and contribute on actual wage base within local floor/cap for all employees incl. foreigners.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Social Insurance Law Art. 58; Interim Measures for Foreigners in Social Insurance (2011); Regulations on Housing Provident Fund

mandatoryPolicies.name: Wage payment policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Monthly payment in RMB, written wage statements, lawful deductions only, OT pay base, records kept 2+ years.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Interim Provisions on Wage Payment (1994); Shanghai Enterprise Wage Payment Measures (effective 1 Aug 2026); Shenzhen Employee Wage Payment Regulations

mandatoryPolicies.name: Confidentiality, IP assignment and non-compete agreements
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Confidentiality for all R&D/FAE staff; non-competes only for eligible staff with monthly compensation; trade-secret protective measures to qualify under AUCL.
mandatoryPolicies.source: LCL Arts. 23-24; Anti-Unfair Competition Law; MOHRSS Enterprise Non-Compete Compliance Guidelines (Sept 2025)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Inventor reward and remuneration policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Agree reward/remuneration for service inventions; without a policy, statutory defaults apply under the Patent Law Implementing Rules.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Patent Law Arts. 6, 15; Patent Law Implementing Rules (revised 2023)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Work safety and occupational health
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Safety responsibility system, training, hazard notices, occupational health exams (pre-, on- and exit-job) for hazardous positions in labs/test facilities.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Work Safety Law (2021); Occupational Disease Prevention Law

mandatoryPolicies.name: Anti-discrimination in recruitment
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: No discrimination by gender, ethnicity, religion, disability, infectious-disease carrier status or rural origin; no hepatitis B testing in pre-employment exams.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Employment Promotion Law Arts. 26-31; 2010 MOHRSS/MOE/MOH Notice on hepatitis B testing

mandatoryPolicies.name: Economic layoff procedure
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: For 20+ or 10%+ reductions: 30-day explanation to union/all staff, labor bureau report, priority retention and rehire rules.
mandatoryPolicies.source: LCL Art. 41; Provisions on Economic Layoffs; Shanghai 沪人社规〔2026〕14号 (from Aug 2026)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Employee equity plan FX registration
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: RSU/option/ESPP plans of overseas-listed parents must be registered with SAFE via a domestic agent (usually the WFOE), with change registrations and periodic filings, before employees participate.
mandatoryPolicies.source: SAFE Circular 7 (Hui Fa [2012] No. 7)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Labor dispatch compliance
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Dispatched workers only in temporary, auxiliary or substitute positions and max 10% of total workforce; equal pay for equal work.
mandatoryPolicies.source: LCL Arts. 63, 66; Interim Provisions on Labor Dispatch (2014)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Retirement handling procedure
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Track new statutory retirement ages, handle voluntary early (3 months' notice by employee) and agreed deferred retirement in writing, and apply for pension on time.
mandatoryPolicies.source: NPCSC Decision on Gradually Raising Statutory Retirement Age (2024); Interim Measures on Flexible Retirement (effective 1 Jan 2025)

hiring.detail: Remove gender, marital/childbearing, ethnicity, religion and health-status criteria; do not ask women about marriage or pregnancy plans; avoid hard age caps in ads.
hiring.cite: Employment Promotion Law Arts. 26-31; Women's Rights Law (2022) Art. 43

hiring.req: No hepatitis B or pregnancy testing
hiring.detail: Pre-employment medicals must exclude HBV markers (unless a specific law requires) and pregnancy tests; brief clinics accordingly.
hiring.cite: 2010 MOHRSS/MOE/MOH Notice; Women's Rights Law Art. 43

hiring.detail: Give a candidate privacy notice; obtain consent for background checks and reference calls; sign entrusted-processing agreements with recruiters and screening vendors; no official criminal-record checks are available to private employers.

hiring.req: Confirm candidate is free of prior employment
hiring.detail: Collect the prior employer's termination certificate and check non-compete/confidentiality obligations, especially for hires from domestic chip firms; hiring someone still bound elsewhere creates joint liability.
Offers are binding pre-contract commitments; execute the Chinese/bilingual labor contract on or before day one and never later than one month.
hiring.cite: LCL Arts. 10, 82; SPC Interpretation II Arts. 6-7

hiring.detail: Match probation length to contract term, pay at least 80% of salary, and give written, measurable hiring criteria that the employee acknowledges.

Obtain Foreigner's Work Permit (A/B/C tiers), Z visa and residence permit (within 30 days of entry) before work; foreign contracts max 5 years. Interpretation II Art. 4 recognizes employment only for foreigners with PR or valid permits.
hiring.cite: Exit-Entry Administration Law; Administrative Provisions on Employment of Foreigners; SPC Interpretation II Art. 4

hiring.detail: Coordinate with trade compliance on US persons assigned to PRC fab-support work (EAR 744.6) and on access to controlled technology before offers are finalized.
hiring.cite: US EAR 15 CFR 744.6; company trade-control policy

onboarding.detail: Both parties sign; give the employee a copy and keep proof of delivery; calendar the expiry date and count of fixed terms.

onboarding.req: Social insurance and housing fund registration
onboarding.detail: Register within 30 days of hire in the city of employment (Shanghai or Shenzhen) on the correct base; include foreigners.
onboarding.cite: Social Insurance Law Art. 58; Housing Provident Fund Regulations

onboarding.detail: Deliver the democratically adopted Chinese handbook and obtain signed or electronic acknowledgement; repeat for each amendment.
Provide the employee PI handling notice; obtain separate consents for sensitive PI (e.g., health, biometrics, bank data) and transfer to US HQ/global HRIS.
Sign confidentiality and invention assignment agreements for all R&D and FAE staff; sign non-competes only for eligible roles; include inventor reward policy.
Pre-job occupational health exams for lab/test roles with chemical, radiation or noise exposure; keep records.
Arrange transfer of the employee's personnel file (dang'an) to a talent service center or HR agency used by the WFOE.
Add new grantees to the SAFE Circular 7 registration and brief them on IIT withholding at vest/exercise and FX repatriation.

payAndPayroll.req: Monthly RMB payment with wage statements
payAndPayroll.detail: Pay on a fixed date at least monthly; provide itemized statements; deductions for employee-caused losses max 20% of monthly wage and not below minimum wage.
payAndPayroll.cite: Labor Law Art. 50; Interim Provisions on Wage Payment Arts. 5-6, 16

payAndPayroll.detail: Shanghai RMB 2,740/month (net of employee SI/HF contributions and allowances); Shenzhen RMB 2,700/month from 1 Sept 2026.
payAndPayroll.cite: Shanghai 沪人社规〔2025〕10号; Guangdong minimum wage notice (2026)

payAndPayroll.detail: Use contractual normal monthly wage divided by 21.75 (daily) or 174 (hourly); 150/200/300% premiums; Shanghai 2026 measures exclude year-end bonus and meal/transport/housing allowances from the OT base.
payAndPayroll.cite: Labor Law Art. 44; MOHRSS 2025 working-time notice; Shanghai Enterprise Wage Payment Measures (2026)

payAndPayroll.detail: Use cumulative withholding with special additional deductions (e.g., child education, infant care RMB 2,000/child/month, elderly support); file and pay by the 15th of the following month.
payAndPayroll.cite: Individual Income Tax Law; STA cumulative withholding rules

payAndPayroll.detail: Year-end bonus may be taxed separately from monthly salary (once per year per employee) through 31 Dec 2027; model both options.

WFOE withholds IIT on RSU vest/option exercise/ESPP discount as wages; listed-company equity income may be taxed separately from other wages through 31 Dec 2027; file plan documents with local tax bureau.
payAndPayroll.cite: Caishui [2005] No. 35; Caishui [2018] No. 164; MOF/STA Announcement 2023 No. 25

payAndPayroll.detail: Foreign employees may choose tax-exempt housing, language and children's education allowances (through 31 Dec 2027) or special additional deductions, not both.
Equal pay for equal work, including dispatched workers; no gender pay discrimination.
Salary reductions or structure changes require written agreement; unilateral cuts support Art. 38 resignation with severance.

timeAndLeave.detail: 8 h/day, 40 h/week; OT after consulting the union and employee, max 36 h/month; track OT for engineers and FAEs during tape-outs or customer escalations.
Apply to the local HR bureau for flexible hours for sales/FAE/senior staff or comprehensive hours for shift/test roles; without approval standard OT rules apply.
timeAndLeave.cite: 1994 MOL Measures on Approval of Non-standard Working Hours; local implementation rules

timeAndLeave.detail: Follow the State Council annual schedule (13 statutory days since 2025); holiday work at 300% with no time-off substitution.
timeAndLeave.cite: National Holidays Regulations (amended Nov 2024); Labor Law Art. 44

timeAndLeave.detail: Verify cumulative service at hire; schedule leave; pay 300% for untaken leave unless employee waived in writing; pro-rate on exit.
timeAndLeave.cite: Regulations on Paid Annual Leave for Employees; 2008 Implementation Measures

timeAndLeave.req: Sick leave and medical treatment period
timeAndLeave.detail: Apply service-based medical periods; Shanghai: set sick pay in contract/handbook after 15 Aug 2026 lapse of local notices (floor 80% of minimum wage); Shenzhen: at least 60% of normal wage.
timeAndLeave.cite: MOL 1994 Medical Treatment Period Provisions; Shanghai 沪府发〔2015〕40号; Shenzhen Employee Wage Payment Regulations

timeAndLeave.detail: Shanghai: 158 days maternity, 10 days paternity, 5 days/yr childcare leave; Guangdong: 178 days, 15 days paternity, 10 days/yr childcare leave; top up maternity allowance to salary where required.
timeAndLeave.cite: Special Provisions on Labor Protection of Female Employees; Shanghai and Guangdong Population and Family Planning Regulations

timeAndLeave.detail: National 3 days marriage leave; Shanghai 10 days; bereavement 1-3 days; paid at normal wage.
timeAndLeave.cite: 1980 State notice on marriage and bereavement leave; local regulations

timeAndLeave.detail: No extended hours or night work from 7 months' pregnancy; prenatal visits count as working time; 1 hour/day nursing break until child's first birthday.
timeAndLeave.cite: Special Provisions on Labor Protection of Female Employees Arts. 6, 9

benefits.detail: Contribute on the employee's actual prior-year average wage within the city floor/cap; cash-in-lieu or waiver agreements are void and expose the employer to back contributions and Art. 38 resignations.
benefits.cite: Social Insurance Law; SPC Interpretation II Art. 19

benefits.detail: Shanghai base resets 1 July (2026-27: RMB 7,546-37,731, top-up due by 30 Sept 2026); Shenzhen/Guangdong bases also reset around July, verify current figures before payroll cut-over.
Mandatory for PRC nationals; Shanghai basic rate 5-7% each side (supplementary fund optional), Shenzhen 5-12%; foreigners generally may opt in (verify local rule).
benefits.cite: Regulations on Management of Housing Provident Fund; local HF center rules

benefits.detail: Enroll foreign employees; no US-China totalization agreement, so US expats pay both unless exempt under another country's agreement; pension account can be refunded on leaving China.
benefits.cite: Interim Measures for Foreigners Employed in China Participating in Social Insurance (2011)

benefits.detail: Apply for work injury recognition within 30 days of an accident or occupational disease diagnosis; sudden death at work within 48 hours of onset counts as work injury.
benefits.cite: Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance Arts. 15, 17

benefits.detail: Enterprise annuity and supplementary medical insurance are optional but common in MNC tech packages; commercial medical must not replace statutory coverage.
Shanghai (June-Sept) and Guangdong (June-Oct) require allowances for outdoor or non-cooled workplaces; typically not office engineers, but check lab/field roles.
benefits.cite: Shanghai 沪人社规〔2019〕19号; Guangdong high-temperature rules

performanceAndConduct.detail: Define 'serious violations' concretely in a handbook adopted through democratic procedure; global Code of Conduct must be localized and acknowledged to support Art. 39 dismissals.
Incompetence dismissal requires objective, communicated standards, evidence of failure, training or job adjustment, then renewed failure, plus 30 days' notice or pay in lieu and N.
Maintain policy, training, confidential reporting channel, investigation and discipline; failures expose the employer to liability and reputational harm.
performanceAndConduct.cite: Women's Rights Law (2022) Art. 25; Civil Code Art. 1010

performanceAndConduct.detail: Changes to role, location or pay need written agreement unless the contract reasonably permits and the change is fair; Shanghai-Shenzhen transfers need consent.
Monitor company systems and devices only with prior notice in handbook/privacy notice, proportionate to purpose; avoid personal chat content and covert monitoring.
Train on commercial bribery (gifts, hospitality, customer travel) and anti-kickback rules; misconduct can be a serious violation if in handbook.
Collect only necessary data, notify under PIPL, avoid removing evidence abroad without transfer compliance, and brief counsel on state-secret and counter-espionage sensitivities.
performanceAndConduct.cite: PIPL; Data Security Law; Counter-Espionage Law (2023)

performanceAndConduct.detail: Only for employer-funded professional technical training; liquidated damages capped at unamortized training cost; courts weigh actual losses and service completed.
performanceAndConduct.cite: LCL Art. 22; SPC Interpretation II Art. 12

termination.detail: Mutual agreement (Art. 36), fault (Art. 39), no-fault (Art. 40), economic layoff (Art. 41) or expiry (Art. 44); document evidence before acting.
Give written notice to the enterprise union (or, where none, the local/district union per local practice) before unilateral termination; failure makes termination unlawful unless cured before suit.

No Art. 40/41 termination or expiry during pregnancy/maternity/nursing, medical treatment period, occupational disease exposure without exit exam, work injury, or 15+ years' service within 5 years of the (now rising) retirement age; contracts auto-extend.
termination.cite: LCL Arts. 42, 45; SPC Interpretation II Art. 17

termination.req: Notice or pay in lieu for Art. 40
termination.detail: 30 days' written notice or one month's wage in lieu, plus N.
Non-renewal at expiry triggers N unless the employee declines renewal on equal or better terms; after two fixed terms the employee can demand open-ended.
2N damages or reinstatement with back pay; reinstatement refused only where objectively impossible (e.g., pension receipt, contract expired, dissolution, conflicting new job).
termination.cite: LCL Arts. 48, 87; SPC Interpretation II Arts. 16, 18

termination.detail: Most MNC exits use mutual termination agreements with an enhanced package; document that the employer proposed to reflect N floor.
Contract ends when the employee starts receiving pension; with rising retirement ages, reaching the old age no longer suffices.
termination.cite: LCL Art. 44; LCL Implementing Regulations Art. 21; SPC Interpretation II

exit.detail: Issue at termination, stating contract term, termination date, position and years of service; omit negative reasons unless required.
exit.cite: LCL Art. 50; LCL Implementing Regulations Art. 24

exit.req: Transfer file and social insurance within 15 days
exit.detail: Complete personnel file transfer and social insurance/housing fund transfer or suspension within 15 days of termination.
Pay final wages, untaken annual leave (300%) and any bonus due at termination; pay economic compensation upon completion of handover.
exit.cite: Interim Provisions on Wage Payment Art. 9; LCL Art. 50

exit.detail: Decide at exit whether to activate (start monthly payments, notify the employee of scope and trade secrets involved) or release; if released during the restriction, pay 3 extra months of compensation.
exit.cite: LCL Art. 24; SPC Interpretation (I) Arts. 36-39; MOHRSS Non-Compete Guidelines (2025)

exit.detail: Handover checklist; return devices, lab notebooks and confidential data; certify deletion from personal devices; revoke access.
Keep terminated contract texts and termination documents at least 2 years.
Update SAFE Circular 7 registration for departing participants; ensure post-exit vesting/exercise proceeds are repatriated and taxed.

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: Rely on necessity for HR management under lawfully adopted rules and collective contracts, or contract necessity; document it in the handbook and notice.
Separate consent for sensitive PI (health, biometrics, financial accounts, precise ID data), provision to third parties and cross-border transfer, even where HR-necessity applies.

HR-management transfers genuinely necessary for cross-border HR are exempt from security assessment/standard contract/certification; otherwise: security assessment for >1M individuals' PI or >10,000 sensitive PI per year; standard contract filing or certification for 100,000-1M PI or <10,000 sensitive PI.
recordsAndPrivacy.cite: CAC Provisions on Promoting and Regulating Cross-Border Data Flows (2024); Certification Measures (effective 1 Jan 2026)

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: Conduct and keep for 3 years before sensitive PI processing, cross-border transfers, entrusted processing (payroll/benefits vendors) and automated decisions.
Risk-based periodic self-audits; regulator may order third-party audits after incidents; submit rectification plans within 15 working days when required.
recordsAndPrivacy.cite: Measures for PI Protection Compliance Audits (effective 1 May 2025)

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: If processing PI of >1M individuals (usually not from HR data alone for this employer), appoint and register a PIPO with CAC.
recordsAndPrivacy.cite: PIPL Art. 52; CAC PIPO reporting announcement (2025)

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: Face or fingerprint clock-in needs separate consent, an alternative method and PIPIA; file with CAC above 100,000 individuals.
recordsAndPrivacy.cite: Facial Recognition Technology Security Measures (effective 1 Jun 2025)

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: Remediate and notify regulators and affected individuals; amended CSL raises fines and adds individual liability.
recordsAndPrivacy.cite: PIPL Art. 57; Cybersecurity Law (amended, effective 1 Jan 2026); Network Data Security Management Regulations

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: Contracts and termination records 2 years post-exit; wage records 2+ years; PIPIAs 3 years; delete or anonymize when purpose ends.
recordsAndPrivacy.cite: LCL Art. 50; Interim Provisions on Wage Payment Art. 6; PIPL Arts. 19, 47, 56

healthSafety.detail: Designate responsible persons, conduct safety training and hazard checks; enterprises over 100 employees need a safety management function or full-time safety staff.
Hazard notification, protective equipment, and pre-, on- and exit-job health exams for exposed lab/test employees; no termination without exit exam.
healthSafety.cite: Occupational Disease Prevention Law; LCL Art. 42(1); SPC Interpretation II Art. 17

healthSafety.detail: Safe storage, handling and training for chemicals, gases and lasers used in characterization labs.
healthSafety.cite: Regulations on Safe Management of Hazardous Chemicals

healthSafety.detail: Keep pregnant and nursing employees out of prohibited work (e.g., certain chemical exposure) and adjust duties.
healthSafety.cite: Special Provisions on Labor Protection of Female Employees (2012) Annex

healthSafety.detail: Maintain coverage; report injuries within 30 days; uninsured employers pay benefits themselves.
Brief employees on device handling, data carried across borders and counter-espionage sensitivities for customer-fab and cross-border travel.
Monitor OT and long-hour cultures during product crunches; sudden death at work counts as work injury, and OT breaches attract labor inspection.
healthSafety.cite: Labor Law Arts. 41, 90; Work Injury Insurance Regulations Art. 15

terminationDeepDive.voluntary: Employee gives 30 days' written notice (3 days in probation); resignation takes effect at the end of notice without employer acceptance, and longer contractual notice is generally unenforceable. There is no statutory garden leave, but the employer can agree to an earlier release date (pay to that date); employee 'buyouts' of notice are not a statutory concept and liquidated damages are allowed only for service-period (training) and non-compete breaches. Immediate resignation with severance is available where the employer breached (LCL Art. 38). No severance on ordinary resignation; issue a termination certificate and decide on non-compete activation.
terminationDeepDive.involuntary: Only statutory grounds: Art. 39 (failing probation criteria, serious violation of lawfully adopted rules, serious dereliction causing major damage, harmful concurrent employment, fraud, criminal liability) with no notice or severance; Art. 40 (non-work illness after the medical period, proven incompetence after training/reassignment, objective change after failed consultation) with 30 days' notice or pay in lieu plus N. Notify the union first (Art. 43), give written reasons, keep evidence, and respect Art. 42 protected categories. Courts scrutinize evidence closely; wrongful termination costs 2N or reinstatement with back pay, and Interpretation II narrows when reinstatement can be refused.
terminationDeepDive.redundancy: Individual redundancy uses Art. 40(3) (material change in objective circumstances plus good-faith consultation on contract variation) with notice/pay in lieu and N. Economic layoff under Art. 41 (20+ employees, or fewer than 20 but 10%+ of workforce) is limited to bankruptcy reorganization, serious operating difficulty, production change/major technical innovation, or other major objective change; explain 30 days in advance to the union or all employees, consider opinions, report the plan to the labor bureau (Shanghai: notify worker representatives 30 days before filing under 沪人社规〔2026〕14号 from Aug 2026), retain priority groups (long fixed-term or open-ended contracts, sole earners supporting elderly/minors) and rehire laid-off staff first within 6 months. In practice MNCs run voluntary mutual-termination programs to avoid Art. 41 scrutiny.
terminationDeepDive.finalPayTiming: Wages must be paid in full upon termination (Interim Provisions on Wage Payment Art. 9; local rules may allow a few working days - verify Shenzhen); economic compensation is payable when handover is completed (LCL Art. 50). Unpaid wages, OT or severance can be ordered by the labor bureau with additional compensation of 50%-100% of the amount owed (LCL Art. 85); failure to issue termination certificate causing loss attracts damages (Art. 89). Untaken annual leave is paid at 300%.
requiredDocuments: Written termination notice citing the legal ground (plus record of prior union notification for unilateral terminations)
Termination certificate (离职证明) with contract term, termination date, position and years of service, issued at termination
Personnel file transfer and social insurance/housing fund transfer or suspension within 15 days
Final wage statement including untaken leave payout and IIT withholding
Mutual termination agreement (Chinese or bilingual, Chinese prevailing) where negotiated
Non-compete activation notice or written release
Handover checklist and confirmation of return/deletion of confidential information
SAFE Circular 7 participant update for departing equity holders
terminationDeepDive.releaseAgreements: Mutual termination agreements (LCL Art. 36) are market standard and generally enforceable; SPC Interpretation (I) (2020) Art. 35 upholds agreements settling wages, OT and compensation absent fraud, coercion, material misunderstanding or obvious unfairness. No statutory review period or consideration formula, but the agreement should record that the employer proposed termination (making N the floor), a full release, SI/HF handling, non-compete decision, confidentiality and payment schedule. Waivers of social insurance obligations and of mandatory work-injury rights are void (SPC Interpretation II Art. 19).
terminationDeepDive.typicalPackage: Market practice (not law) for tech/semiconductor MNCs in Shanghai and Shenzhen: N+1 to N+3 months, often calculated without the 3x cap for senior engineers, plus pro-rata bonus, untaken annual leave at 300% and sometimes extended medical cover or outplacement. Employees in protected periods (pregnancy, medical treatment period) command materially higher packages, often salary through the end of protection plus N. Treat 2N as the litigation ceiling benchmark.

recentChanges.title: Guangdong/Shenzhen minimum wage increase
recentChanges.detail: From 1 Sept 2026 Shenzhen's minimum wage rose to RMB 2,700/month and RMB 25.4/hour for part-timers (from RMB 2,520); floors for sick pay (80%) and probation pay follow.

recentChanges.title: Shanghai sick-pay notices lapse
recentChanges.detail: Shanghai's 1995 sick-leave pay notice (沪劳保发〔1995〕83号) and 2000 minimum sick-pay notice expired on 15 Aug 2026 without renewal; sick pay now follows contract/handbook terms with a floor of 80% of the minimum wage (about RMB 2,192). Existing contractual or handbook terms still bind, and changes need democratic procedure.

recentChanges.title: Shanghai wage payment, layoff reporting and collective bargaining rules reissued
recentChanges.detail: Shanghai Enterprise Wage Payment Measures reissued (沪人社规〔2026〕10号, effective 1 Aug 2026) defining the OT base; revised economic layoff reporting (沪人社规〔2026〕14号) requiring 30 days' notice to union/worker representatives before filing; new collective bargaining dispute procedure (沪人社规〔2026〕11号).

recentChanges.title: Shanghai 2026-27 social insurance base
recentChanges.detail: From 1 Jul 2026 Shanghai base is RMB 7,546-37,731/month (average wage RMB 12,577), up from RMB 7,460-37,302; retroactive adjustments due by 30 Sept 2026.

recentChanges.title: Amended Cybersecurity Law in force
recentChanges.detail: Amendments adopted 28 Oct 2025 took effect 1 Jan 2026: higher fines (up to RMB 10 million for serious cases), individual liability up to RMB 1 million, explicit PIPL alignment and broader extraterritorial reach.

recentChanges.title: PI outbound transfer certification measures
recentChanges.detail: CAC/SAMR Measures for Certification of Personal Information Outbound Transfers (issued Oct 2025) took effect 1 Jan 2026, completing the security assessment / standard contract / certification trio for transfers of 100,000-1M individuals' PI or under 10,000 sensitive PI.

recentChanges.title: Revised Anti-Unfair Competition Law
recentChanges.detail: Revised AUCL took effect 15 Oct 2025, mainly addressing platform, data and bribery conduct; the trade-secret definition and misappropriation rules were carried forward (verify article renumbering in internal templates).

recentChanges.title: SPC Interpretation II on labor disputes
recentChanges.detail: Effective 1 Sept 2025: social insurance waivers void (Art. 19); non-competes void for staff without trade-secret access or with unreasonable scope, in-employment non-competes enforceable (Arts. 13-14); broader 'consecutive fixed-term' definition for open-ended contracts (Art. 10); double-wage defenses (Art. 7); limits on refusing reinstatement (Art. 16); foreign-employee recognition (Art. 4).

recentChanges.title: MOHRSS Enterprise Non-Compete Compliance Guidelines
recentChanges.detail: Issued 4 Sept 2025: non-competes only for staff with real trade-secret access; compensation at least 30% of prior 12-month average pay (and minimum wage), generally 50% if over one year; geographic scope tied to actual business; liquidated damages generally not over 5x total compensation.

recentChanges.title: PIPO registration deadline
recentChanges.detail: Processors handling PI of more than 1 million individuals had to register their PI protection officer with CAC by 29 Aug 2025; later crossers have 30 working days.

recentChanges.title: Shanghai minimum wage increase
recentChanges.detail: From 1 Jul 2025 Shanghai minimum wage is RMB 2,740/month and RMB 25/hour; no further 2026 adjustment issued as of Sept 2026.

recentChanges.title: Facial recognition security measures
recentChanges.detail: From 1 Jun 2025 face-based attendance/access requires separate consent, a non-biometric alternative, PIPIA and CAC filing above 100,000 individuals.

recentChanges.title: PI protection compliance audit measures
recentChanges.detail: From 1 May 2025, processors of >10M individuals' PI must self-audit every 2 years; others audit on a risk basis; CAC can order third-party audits after incidents.

recentChanges.title: Two extra public holidays and new working-time divisors
recentChanges.detail: Statutory holidays rose from 11 to 13 (Spring Festival Eve, 2 May); MOHRSS notice (人社部发〔2025〕2号) sets 20.67 average working days/month while keeping 21.75 pay days for wage conversion.

recentChanges.title: Gradual retirement age increase
recentChanges.detail: From 1 Jan 2025 over 15 years: men 60 to 63 and female cadres 55 to 58 (1 month every 4 months), female workers 50 to 55 (1 month every 2 months); voluntary early retirement up to 3 years (employee's 3 months' notice) and agreed deferral up to 3 years; minimum pension contribution years rise from 15 to 20 starting 2030 (6 months per year).

watchlist.title: Shanghai sick pay practice after lapse
watchlist.detail: Watch for new municipal guidance or court practice on sick pay and whether employers can lower legacy handbook entitlements.

watchlist.title: Retirement-age step-ups and contribution years
watchlist.detail: Monthly step-ups continue through 2039; minimum contribution years begin rising from 15 toward 20 in 2030. Art. 42 near-retirement protection and contract end dates shift accordingly.

watchlist.title: Local court guidance applying Interpretation II
watchlist.detail: Shanghai and Guangdong courts may issue guidance on open-ended contracts after two fixed terms, non-compete scope and reinstatement.

watchlist.title: Family-support leave expansions
watchlist.detail: National fertility push is driving provincial extensions of marriage, maternity and childcare leave; monitor Shanghai and Guangdong regulation amendments.

watchlist.title: Data export regime refinements
watchlist.detail: CAC enforcement of PIPL, free-trade-zone negative lists and possible further guidance on HR-data transfers and employee PI standards.

watchlist.title: US-China export-control truce expiry
watchlist.detail: US BIS 50% Affiliates Rule (Sept 2025) was suspended for one year in Nov 2025 alongside Chinese countermeasure suspensions; outcome affects customer screening, staffing of FAEs and sanctions conflicts (verify status with trade team).

watchlist.title: IIT preferential policy sunset
watchlist.detail: Separate taxation of annual bonus and listed-company equity income, and expatriate allowance exemptions, expire 31 Dec 2027 unless extended.

calendar.title: Annual leave reset and prior-year settlement
calendar.detail: Pay 300% for untaken prior-year leave not carried over by agreement; reset entitlements; IIT cumulative withholding restarts.

calendar.title: Union funds (2%)
calendar.detail: Declared monthly/quarterly with tax filings; confirm local collection practice (union funds or preparatory funds where no union) - verify.

calendar.title: Spring Festival and year-end bonus
calendar.detail: Apply State Council schedule and swapped workdays; decide per employee whether to use separate annual-bonus taxation (available through 2027).

calendar.title: IIT annual reconciliation opens
calendar.detail: Employees file 1 Mar - 30 Jun via the Individual Income Tax app; employer supports data queries and may file on behalf where authorized.

calendar.title: SAFE equity plan quarterly filing
calendar.detail: Domestic agent files quarterly equity-plan participation/FX report with SAFE early each quarter (also Jul, Oct, Jan) - verify local deadline.

calendar.title: IIT reconciliation closes and annual reports
calendar.detail: IIT reconciliation deadline 30 Jun; WFOE annual report to SAMR (incl. social insurance data) due 30 Jun; Shenzhen employers declare new SI/HF bases by end-June.

calendar.title: High-temperature allowance season
calendar.detail: Shanghai June-Sept, Guangdong June-Oct for eligible outdoor/non-cooled roles.

calendar.title: Social insurance and housing fund base reset
calendar.detail: New contribution year starts 1 Jul in Shanghai and many cities; update payroll caps/floors and housing fund base.

calendar.title: Base top-up deadline and Guangdong minimum wage
calendar.detail: Shanghai 2026 retroactive SI top-ups due by 30 Sept; Shenzhen minimum wage RMB 2,700 effective 1 Sept 2026.

calendar.title: National Day holiday
calendar.detail: Apply swapped workdays; holiday work at 300%.

calendar.title: Next year's holiday schedule
calendar.detail: State Council typically publishes the following year's schedule in Nov; update HRIS calendars and shift plans.

calendar.title: Year-end compliance sweep
calendar.detail: Ensure annual leave is taken or carried over by agreement; adopt handbook changes via democratic procedure before 1 Jan; track expiring contracts and second fixed terms (open-ended triggers).

gotchas: Treating China as at-will: 'performance' or 'restructuring' exits without an Art. 40 process or mutual agreement lead to 2N or reinstatement orders.
Enforcing a US-drafted global handbook or Code of Conduct that never went through China's democratic procedure and was never acknowledged, so dismissals for 'serious violation' fail.
Missing written contracts or renewals within one month (including auto-renewals and extensions), triggering double wages and deemed open-ended contracts.
Contributing social insurance on a minimum base or paying cash in lieu; since Sept 2025 such agreements are expressly void and employees can resign with severance.
Signing non-competes with all engineers but not paying monthly compensation, or forgetting to release/activate at exit; unpaid compensation lets employees escape the restriction.
Skipping advance union notification or terminating employees in protected periods (pregnancy, medical treatment period, near retirement under the new ages).
Copying employee data to US HRIS, ATS or investigation tools without PIPL notice, separate consent for cross-border transfer and a PIPIA, or assuming the HR exemption covers everything.
Granting RSUs/ESPP without SAFE Circular 7 registration and WFOE IIT withholding, blocking FX repatriation and creating tax penalties.
Assuming Shanghai and Shenzhen rules are the same: leave, sick pay, social insurance bases, minimum wage and layoff filing procedures differ.
Relying on emailed or English-only notices; arbitration requires Chinese-language evidence of delivery and reasons.
semiconductorNotes: US export controls (flag only; trade team leads): EAR 744.6 US-person restrictions bar US citizens/green-card holders from supporting development or production of advanced-node ICs at PRC fabs without a license, affecting FAE staffing and hiring of US persons in China; Entity List customers (and the suspended BIS 50% Affiliates Rule) affect who FAEs may support; releasing controlled technology to PRC nationals in US or third-country R&D sites is a deemed export/re-export requiring licensing.

Counter-Espionage Law (revised, effective 1 Jul 2023) broadened espionage to documents, data and materials related to national security; combined with the Data Security Law ('important data' and industry catalogs) this affects HR investigations, market-intelligence work, border device searches and exit restrictions. Brief travelers and keep HR data inventories that classify any potentially 'important data'.

Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law (2021) and its Implementing Regulations (2025) allow PRC parties to sue for complying with foreign sanctions; HR communications and disciplinary actions tied to US Entity List compliance should be reviewed by counsel to avoid framing that invites countermeasure claims.

China's own export controls (Export Control Law 2020; Dual-Use Items Export Control Regulations effective 1 Dec 2024; catalogue of technologies restricted from export) can restrict engineers transferring PRC-developed technology abroad, including in R&D collaboration with US teams.

Talent competition from state-backed domestic chip firms is intense: use confidentiality and invention assignment for all R&D, eligible-only non-competes with 30-50% monthly compensation per 2025 MOHRSS Guidelines, exit data-return certifications, and an inventor reward policy (Patent Law Art. 15) to avoid statutory default rewards.

Taiwan talent (reverse view): Taiwanese engineers can work in the mainland without PRC work permits, but Taiwan restricts PRC-linked recruitment in Taiwan and requires approval for mainland travel by staff handling designated core key technologies; verify candidates' Taiwan obligations and prior-employer trade-secret exposure before hiring.

RSUs/ESPP: register the plan with SAFE under Circular 7 through the WFOE or a qualified agent, maintain a special FX account for proceeds, update registrations for material changes, and withhold IIT at vest/exercise (separate taxation available through 2027); ESPP payroll contributions cannot be remitted abroad without the registration.

Shift and lab work: test/validation labs running 24/7 need approved comprehensive working hours or full OT pay; exposure to chemicals and lasers triggers occupational health exams and blocks termination without exit exams.
